target_customer: Plastic recyclers and brand owners buying recycled PET and polyurethane inputs
problem: Mechanical recycling degrades plastic, so engineered enzymes depolymerise PET into monomers for virgin-quality recycled resin.
business_model: Technology developer funded by grants and equity, aiming at licensing or process deployment

founders.name: Johan Kers
education: Postdoctoral fellowship, Stanford University School of Medicine

founders.name: Emily Duncan
founders.background_notes: Listed as COO and PhD on the company site; background not found

competitors.name: Carbios
competitors.what: Enzymatic PET biorecycling with demonstration plant
competitors.traction_then: Demonstration plant launched 2021-09 per a funding article
competitors.funding_then: EUR 14.5M share placing for the demonstration plant

technical_complexity.rationale: Engineering enzymes that depolymerise PET and polyurethane at industrial rates is research-grade work.

defensibility.rationale: Enzyme IP and an NREL patent license give some protection, but a well funded competitor was already ahead.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; incumbents progressed on their own plants.

market_need_then: Plastic waste regulation and brand recycled-content targets; the company claims 70% lower emissions than virgin plastic (company claim).

identity.visual_style: Science and climate positioning, 'AI native' tagline

brand_strength.rationale: Little sourced press about the brand; name is a tree word plus Biosciences.

outcome_analysis: Birch is active and funded largely by non-dilutive grants: NSF SBIR Phase I and II, a DOE Phase II, a DARPA award and an NREL licence per its site. Equity funding is poorly documented and aggregators disagree, so the trajectory beyond grants is unclear. The science is hard and capital needs are high.
notes: Unverified equity: CB Insights lists $4.42M across seven rounds with a seed dated 2025-10, PitchBook lists a seed 2023-04; conflicting so not recorded. DOE SBIR Phase II (about $1.9M per a single listing) and DARPA, Amazon Bedrock awards are on the company site without verified amounts or dates. Carbios date from search result summary.
